question.problem:
Find the intersection point of the line $l$ and the plane $Π$ with equations

$$
l:\frac{x+2}{3}=\frac{y+1}{2}=\frac{z}{4},\,Π:r\cdot ⟨3,-1,2⟩=25.
$$
question.worked_solution:
From the equation of the line $l$, we know that it passes through the point $A(-2,-1,0)$ and it is parallel to the vector $v=⟨3,2,4⟩.$ Therefore, its vector equation is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =⟨-2,-1,0⟩+t⟨3,2,4⟩ \\  & =⟨-2+3t,-1+2t,4t⟩,\end{aligned}
$$

where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$

Now, substituting $r=⟨-2+3t,-1+2t,4t⟩$ into the equation of the plane, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}r\cdot ⟨3,-1,2⟩ & =25 \\ ⟨-2+3t,-1+2t,4t⟩\cdot ⟨3,-1,2⟩ & =25 \\ 3(-2+3t)-(-1+2t)+2(4t) & =25 \\ -6+9t+1-2t+8t & =25 \\ 15t & =30 \\ t & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, to get the position vector $p$ of the intersection point $P,$ we substitute $t=2$ into the equation of the line:

$$
\begin{aligned}p & =⟨-2+3(2),-1+2(2),4(2)⟩ \\  & =⟨4,3,8⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

So, we get $P(4,3,8).$
